subject: Follow-up: SLO/Failover qualification for Solara Health POC
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Ng <alyssa@solarahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-30 21:20:00 +0000
Subject: Recap + proposed SLO probes after today's demo

Alyssa — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and the concrete asks we committed to: 

- Goal: validate failover behavior and steady-state error budget under your expected peak (Solara: ~1.2k concurrent sessions during business hours).
- Hyperscaler comparison: you asked for deterministic behaviors under regional outage and per-minute rate-limit conditions. We'll provide a short matrix showing how Redwood falls back to quantized model variants and how major hyperscalers handle similar failovers.

Action items (owners & next steps):
1) Redwood to run 3 probe types against your staging workload: steady QPS at 1.2k, burst to 3k, and simulated region failover. Owner: Ben Carter. Deliverable: CSV of latency percentiles + error codes. ETA: 6/4.
2) Provide SLO matrix that maps product-level SLOs (p99 latency, availability, per-minute rate limits) to Redwood config knobs (batch windows, cache TTL, fallback policy). Owner: Jonas (attached). ETA: 6/1.
3) Share Doc link with proposed tests and a minimal harness you can run from Solara to validate behavior locally. Owner: Marissa — will upload the harness and instructions. ETA: 6/2.

I attached an initial SLO-matrix and a heatmap comparing expected failover behaviors vs. the two hyperscaler endpoints you mentioned. Please confirm these test priorities or flag anything missing.

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
https://redwood.ai/

Attachments: SLO-matrix-solara-v1.xlsx (xlsx), redwood-hyperscaler-heatmap.pdf (pdf)

From: Alyssa Ng <alyssa@solarahealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Solara Health Platform Team <platform@solarahealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-31 11:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Recap + proposed SLO probes after today's demo

Jonas — really helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side before you run the probes: 

- For the region failover, please simulate an east-US -> west-US failover (we're multi-AZ in azure-eastus and we want to know how cross-region failover would behave).
- For the burst test, make sure you include a sequence where KV cache is cold (we expect many short-lived sessions during launches).
- Rate limits: our security team insists on observing per-API-key per-minute throttles; please show typical 429 behavior and backoff recommendations.

We can host the harness in our staging and run the client side if that's easier; Marissa's note about the instructions will help.

Two asks from me: can you include expected error-budget consumption assuming a 99.95% availability target, and a suggested fallback policy (e.g., reduced model size + degraded features) that keeps most requests alive?

If you can send the SLO-matrix by EOD Tuesday (6/1) that would be great. We'll sync on the test window for the failover simulation next week.

Best,
Alyssa Ng
Head of Platform Engineering, Solara Health
alyssa@solarahealth.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-05-31 17:44:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Recap + proposed SLO probes after today's demo

Marissa: can you take the staging-harness upload and the runbook? Ben: can you own the failover/run schedule and the latency/error CSVs. I'll prepare the SLO matrix and draft a recommended fallback policy (quantized variant + short-lived samplers).

Deliverables & provisional owners: 
- SLO matrix + error-budget calc (Jonas) — new ETA: 2027-06-01 23:00Z
- Staging harness + run instructions (Marissa) — ETA: 2027-06-02 18:00Z
- Failover + burst probes and raw CSV output (Ben) — ETA: 2027-06-04 23:59Z

Flagging Ben for any infra constraints (we may need a temporary dedicated pool during the burst test). Alyssa — if you prefer to run the client side from Solara staging, say so and we'll hand over the harness.

Thanks — Jonas

---
Jonas Weber
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alyssa Ng <alyssa@solarahealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-02 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Recap + proposed SLO probes after today's demo

Jonas / Marissa / Ben — thanks for the quick turn. We will run the client side from our staging environment to avoid cross-account network variables. Confirming: 

- Solara will accept the harness and instructions from Marissa (please drop the Drive link when ready).
- Ben, we request the failover probe window be scheduled during our staging-maintenance window: 2027-06-07 02:00–05:00 UTC. Is that workable? We want a full east->west region cutover in that period.
- Jonas, for the error-budget calc please include both 99.95% and 99.9% baselines so our SREs can compare tolerance tradeoffs.

Once we have the CSVs and the heatmap, we'll schedule a follow-up to review the results and pick a candidate fallback policy. Prefer 30–45 minute review slot next week.

Alyssa
Alyssa Ng
Head of Platform Engineering, Solara Health
alyssa@solarahealth.com
